key_insight: Fun-DDPS combines a function-space diffusion prior with a differentiable neural-operator surrogate to decouple geometry/parameter generation from physics solvers, enabling fast, accurate forward predictions and well-calibrated inverse/posterior sampling for subsurface CCS problems.
problem_solved: Addresses ill-posed inverse problems in carbon storage where sparse observations and costly PDE solvers make uncertainty-aware parameter estimation and posterior sampling impractical.
method: Train a single-channel function-space diffusion model to learn a prior over geological fields (geomodels) rather than finite-dimensional parameter vectors.
Use a differentiable neural operator surrogate (fast, PDE-aware forward model) to map generated geomodels to observable flow/pressure fields for both forward prediction and likelihood evaluation.

Decouple sampling and physics by combining diffusion-based prior samples with neural-operator-driven conditioning or gradient-based posterior refinement to produce calibrated inverse solutions and uncertainty quantification.
impact: Provides a scalable template for combining generative diffusion priors and neural operators to solve expensive, ill-posed physical inverse problems — useful for ML researchers building physics-aware generative/inverse pipelines and practitioners needing fast uncertainty-aware predictions.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: function-space diffusion prior -> neural-operator surrogate -> conditioning/posterior sampling

paper_title: Function-Space Decoupled Diffusion for Forward and Inverse Modeling in Carbon Capture and Storage
paper_authors: Xin Ju, Jiachen Yao, Anima Anandkumar, Sally M. Benson, Gege Wen
